quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: Section 4 runs in our favour and meets the fallback on its material terms, indeed most of the preferred position. The Works (all work product required by a Statement of Work) "are the property of Company" once invoiced and paid (p0017), and on termination Contractor "hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress" (p0033), so ownership of deliverables vests in Clear Capital rather than being licensed. Contractor retains only its own pre-existing proprietary works, tools, methodologies and know-how not created for us (p0020) — the permitted vendor-retention carve-out — and where that material is embedded in the Works we hold a royalty-free, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivatives for our business operations (p0021), reinforced by our post-payment/post-termination right to modify the software and engage others to do so without further payment (p0022). No joint ownership is created, no Clear Capital IP or data is assigned to Contractor, and there is no standing vendor licence in our data: Confidential Information (including our records, data and reports) may not be used or disclosed by Contractor without our express prior written permission (p0040), so the Customer-Data element is satisfied by prohibition rather than an over-broad processing licence. Sub-preferred points noted but not redlined: the embedded-IP licence is not expressly labelled "irrevocable" or "worldwide" (it is perpetual and untethered to any revocation or territorial mechanic elsewhere in the Agreement), there is no affirmative sentence confirming we retain all rights in our data, and §4(b)(ii) limits resale/use of Contractor's administrative records to the software we receive. These are wording gaps short of the preferred position, not material failures, so we accept the clause as drafted.

verification.notes: The fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: a single added sentence supplies the mutual successor carve-out on written notice, while the original mutual consent requirement and the "not unreasonably withheld" standard survive verbatim to cover all other assignments. The preferred level is not reached: there is no affiliate carve-out for Clear Capital, no competitor bar on RadialSpark, and the carve-out is mutual so RadialSpark can now assign to a successor without Clear Capital's consent. That is acceptable here only because the drafter expressly targeted the fallback, which itself mandates mutuality; the mutual exception is therefore not an intent failure. Minimality holds: one inserted sentence, no deletions, no survival tail, no expense or procedural extras, and no duplication of the existing consent mechanic. The words "upon written notice to the other party" are required by the fallback element rather than surplus. Intent is preserved: the subcontracting restriction, the consent standard and all cross-references remain intact, no defined term is left dangling, and no retained sentence contradicts the new carve-out (the carve-out is drafted as an express exception to "the foregoing consent requirement"). Classification as a deviation is supportable — before the edit the clause failed the fallback elements requiring a successor right on notice — though note this is not walk-away territory, since the original consent requirement was mutual and reasonableness-qualified rather than a blanket prohibition. quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The only licence grant to us is Section 4(c) (p0021). It is helpfully perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, but "Company" is defined as Clear Capital alone (p0002), so the grant does not reach our affiliates and there is no path to add them by notice. Nor is the licence transferable: Section 10 (p0042) bars either party from assigning or transferring the Agreement or its rights without the other's prior written consent, so the licence would not follow us into a merger or acquisition. Both fallback elements therefore fail on material terms. We propose the shortest fallback cure: one sentence extending the licence to affiliates identified by written notice and permitting transfer to an M&A successor without Contractor's approval. We have not pressed the preferred elements (contractor coverage, express irrevocability) here.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The foregoing license also extends to any affiliate of Company identified in a written notice to Contractor". elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 4(c) nor the inserted sentence names contractors acting on Company's behalf. The pre-existing "right to grant a sublicense" is a discretionary onward-grant mechanic, not an extension of the grant to Company's contractors. elements.evidence: The inserted sentence permits transfer only "to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction". Read literally that is narrower than transferability to Customer's successors generally (e.g. successors by reorganisation or operation of law); the preferred element would need "successors and assigns" or equivalent.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "The foregoing license also extends to any affiliate of Company identified in a written notice to Contractor" — coverage is triggered by written notice, exactly the fallback mechanic, and Company does not already include affiliates so there is no duplicate coverage.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "...and is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction without Contractor's approval." The express "without Contractor's approval" carve-out neutralises the Section 10 consent bar for this transfer without a broad notwithstanding override.

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: both atomic elements are delivered in one inserted sentence with operative, unconditional language and no undefined trigger. Preferred level fails on three elements — no extension to contractors acting on Company's behalf, no express irrevocability in the Section 4(c) grant, and a transfer right limited to M&A successors rather than successors generally. The margin comment correctly declines to press these, so the fallback is the operative target. Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, the favourable existing "royalty-free, non-exclusive perpetual" and sublicence language is retained, Section 10 is left intact, and no survival tail, expense, procedure or other extra requirement is bolted on. The added "without Contractor's approval" is necessary rather than surplus because Section 10 would otherwise block the M&A transfer, and the playbook prefers this direct permission over a broad notwithstanding override. Intent is preserved: the retained Section 10 mutual consent regime continues to govern assignment of the Agreement generally, and the new sentence operates as a specific, Customer-side carve-out for the Section 4(c) licence only — it does not create any new Vendor assignment exception, and it leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term ("affiliate" is used in its ordinary sense, consistent with the notice mechanic). Optional polish, not a defect: if the counterparty accepts, consider defining "Affiliate" and adding "irrevocable" plus contractor coverage to move from fallback to the preferred position.

rationale: Section 6 gives a convenience right only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding" — i.e. exactly when no work is being performed. The same gating condition works in our favour on the Vendor side: Contractor cannot walk away while a Statement of Work is outstanding, so the "no Vendor convenience right during a committed term" element is already met and we have not disturbed it. elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.

elements.evidence: Retained 6(a) grants the mutual no-cause right only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding"; Contractor therefore has no convenience exit while an engagement (the committed term under this MSA) is live. The insertion does not extend any Contractor right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.

verification.notes: All four preferred elements are satisfied: the single inserted sentence supplies a Company-only convenience right over the Agreement or any Statement of Work, 30 days' written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, while retained 6(a) already confines Contractor's no-cause right to periods with no outstanding Statement of Work. The fallback level is incomplete (30-day notice rather than 60–90 days; Contractor's no-cause right is not term-end-only and carries only 15 days' notice), but that is irrelevant because the preferred checklist is fully met and position-completeness requires only one level. Minimal: one concise insertion, no deletion of existing language, no 'in whole or in part' surplus (no Order Form/partial-termination structure requires it), no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or other model-language extras, and no duplication of the retained 6(a) or 6(b) mechanics. Preserves intent: the mutual 15-day no-SOW right in 6(a), the material-breach right and fee/Works-in-progress consequences in 6(b), and all defined terms (Agreement, Statement of Work, Contractor, Company) survive without contradiction; 'In addition' makes clear the new right is cumulative rather than displacing 6(a). Finding classification of 'deviation' is supportable: before the edit Company had no convenience exit while any Statement of Work was live and no prepaid-fee refund, failing both levels on the Customer side.

With no audit right binding us, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain, so our position is better than the preferred checklist and no redline is warranted; we should not volunteer audit machinery. If RadialSpark later requests verification rights, we would cap them at the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%).

verification.notes: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York substantive law plus exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction over all Disputes. The original clause was a genuine deviation (Arizona law, walk-away-adjacent mandatory USA&M arbitration with confirmation venue keyed to the respondent's residence), so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale-only note. Minimality holds. In Section 11 only the words "the Arizona" were swapped for "the State of New York"; the severability sentence and the conflict-of-laws tail survive. In Section 19 the deletions (the arbitration submission and the award-confirmation sentence) are the operative arbitration mechanic itself, which had to be converted to reach the courts element, and the heading rename from "Arbitration" to "Dispute Resolution" is required so no dangling arbitration reference remains. No survival tail, fee-shifting, jury waiver, service-of-process, or injunctive-relief boilerplate was added. Intent preserved: the Dispute definition (common law, statutory and equitable claims, pre- and post-dating the Agreement, limbs (b) and (c)) is retained verbatim, so the breadth of covered disputes is unchanged; only the forum changed. Signature block and Effective Date references are untouched. Drafting note (not a failure): the retained lead-in "Except as otherwise specified below" now points to whatever carve-outs remain in the un-quoted portion of Section 19; if the deleted award-confirmation sentence was the only "below" exception, delete those four words or confirm a surviving carve-out so the lead-in does not dangle. We did not press the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, data protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement carve-outs or the payment-obligations exclusion.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: the cap is mutual, restated on a 12-months-of-fees basis, and one inserted mutual sentence places indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap. The claimed 'deviation' status and fallback target are correct. Preferred remains short on five elements the drafter must add if escalating: (i) the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor and 'paid or payable' basis; (ii) data protection and security breach carve-out; (iii) fraud carve-out; (iv) infringement of the other party's IP carve-out; (v) an express statement that Company's payment obligations are not 'damages' subject to the cap (currently Company's cap could be read to limit its own fee-payment exposure). Minimality holds: only the fee-basis words and one carve-out sentence changed; deletion of 'FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES' was necessary to convert the basis to 12 months of fees, and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added. Intent preserved: 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the Contractor-side 'performance of Services under a Statement of Work' scope survive without contradiction, and the new carve-out sentence coexists with the retained Paragraph 9 exception. Note (advisory, pre-existing and not caused by this edit): the 'PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF' cross-reference points to the independent-contractor provision and is effectively dangling as a liability exception; consider correcting or deleting it in a separate pass rather than in this fallback redline.
